candidates.severity: unassigned; source-established historical-visibility mismatch under an exact prior-lead and disclosure sequence
candidates.classification: 95e revisit of the earlier correction-source namespace finding, including both reducer and view readers; not a new unique historical defect.
candidates.trace: An eligible public-threat disclosure creates or updates PublicThreatDisclosure under a public-threat:<character>:<public-case> ID, recording observer minute. It marks uncorrected leads for the same observer/public case and a different exact location by storing that disclosure ID in InvestigationLead.corrected_by. The exact-site reducer reader, however, resolves nonempty corrected_by only through InvestigationLead.id and needs that lead row and its recorded_at; if no same-ID correction lead exists it returns false. The view reader independently performs the same lead-table-only lookup. The actual exact-site, occupancy and contextual-actor projection paths consume these predicates.
candidates.conditional_example: Assume an admitted exact lead for site A was recorded at minute 100, a valid public disclosure of different true site B occurs at minute 200 and changes the lead reference, no InvestigationLead with the disclosure ID exists, no other valid exact lead supplies A, and all site/alias/occupancy guards otherwise succeed. A later historical query at observer minute 150 should be able to use the still-then-live A lead, but the recorded reference cannot supply a correction time and the selected reducer and view predicates reject it. The earlier 059 Lens11/Lens12 records identified this same writer/reader mismatch; this is an independent source-based revisit, not an executed chronology or new unique defect.
candidates.related_observation: The safe lead label intentionally falls back to generic later-account prose if the lead lookup fails; it is a privacy projection, not by itself proof of a separate bug. The public disclosure row is updated in place when a later disclosure changes its payload, including learned_at. Therefore simply looking up that mutable field as an immutable first-correction timestamp would require a separate chronology policy; source does not establish that such a proposed remedy is sufficient.
candidates.connected_repair: After the audit gate choose one canonical typed correction identity and immutable observer-frontier owner for all lead, disclosure and correction writers plus reducer/view/history/presence consumers. Preserve real historical visibility before a correction, actual supersession afterward, unrelated observers and cases, safe disclosure labels, collisions and legitimate manual/generated modes. Do not add compatibility fallback or fabricate a time from a mutable latest-disclosure field.
candidates.later_acceptance: After separately authorized implementation and validation, assess initial and repeated public disclosure, prior and post-correction observer times, exact site/actor visibility, colliding or absent references, same/different observers and private safe projections using existing appropriate gates. None ran.
candidates.discovery: partial; all correction writers/readers, actual admitted chronology, stable first-frontier policy and global historical aliases remain open
